verdict.rationale: Exa's own docs name two official SDKs, `exa-py` and `exa-js`, both reading `EXA_API_KEY` from the environment. The exa-js GitHub repo documents agent-oriented usage: a `webSearch()` tool for OpenAI and Anthropic loops, `streamSearch` with OpenAI-style chunks, `answer` with citations, and `outputSchema` constraints. Missing for 10: any documented depth for exa-py beyond its install line, and independent or hands-on corroboration of building with the SDKs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Prefer the official SDKs, `exa-py` (`pip install exa-py`) and `exa-js` (`npm install exa-js`); both read `EXA_API_KEY` from the environment.
Use Exa as a `web_search` tool in an OpenAI or Anthropic loop. Call `webSearch()` with no arguments to get Exa's recommended settings for agentic search
Search streaming is available via `streamSearch(...)`, which yields OpenAI-style chat completion chunks.
`systemPrompt` and `outputSchema` are supported on every search type.
